title: Uptime orchestration: mini-sprints & field notes for cross-team reliability experiments
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick working doc for a set of 3-week mini-sprints to test low-friction reliability interventions across product, infra, platform, and CS.
- Goal: validate a small set of controls that reliably improve customer-visible availability and tail latency without major infra spend.
- Audience: SRE leads, PMs for hosting products (Hosted API / Dedicated), infra/platform eng, observability owners, solutions eng.

What success looks like (hypotheses we want to test):
1) A small set of telemetry-derived alerts + tuned error budget policies reduces P99 tail latency incidents by 30% in pilot services within 6 weeks.
2) Lightweight runbook stitching and a rapid escalation pattern reduces mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for model-serving degradations by ~20%.
3) A staged SLO gating pattern (canary->soft gate->hard gate) prevents regressions during model rollouts in at least 2 product teams.

Scope of mini-sprints (3 parallel lanes):
- Lane A: Telemetry & detection experiments (obs team lead)
  - Target: 2 pilot services (chat generation, embeddings ingestion)
  - Deliverables: sample dashboards, adjusted synthetic probes, new alert scoring rule, incident-to-metric mapping doc
  - Owner: Priya Kapoor
  - Key metrics to capture: request success rate, P50/P90/P99 latency, prefix-cache hit rate, error budget burn rate

- Lane B: Runbook stitching & escalation drills (SRE ops)
  - Target: stitch product runbooks with platform runbooks; create a 5-step 'bridge-to-green' checklist for model-serving incidents
  - Deliverables: consolidated runbook, tabletop drill script, 1-page cheat sheet for oncall rotation
  - Owner: Jonah Li

- Lane C: SLO gating for model rollouts (product + serving runtime)
  - Target: implement soft gating on rollouts in Dedicated staging for one customer flow; validate rollback thresholds and fallback policies
  - Deliverables: rollout policy template, canary metrics panel, rollback automation playbook (manual trigger first iteration)
  - Owner: Alejandro Ruiz

Cadence & milestones (6 week pilot, broken into two 3-week mini-sprints):
- Week 0 (pre-work, 5 days): stakeholder alignment, define pilot services, baseline telemetry collection.
- Mini-sprint 1 (weeks 1-3): implement detection rules, initial runbook stitching, basic gating policy in staging. Run 1 tabletop exercise.
- Review checkpoint (end week 3): collect signals, quick retro, decide go/no-go for iteration changes.
- Mini-sprint 2 (weeks 4-6): iterate on alert thresholds, automate one rollback path, run live drill for bridged runbooks, measure SLO impact on canary traffic.
- Wrap & next steps (end week 6): consolidate docs, produce handoff checklist for scaling, propose metric thresholds for org-wide adoption.

Roles & stakeholders (quick RACI-ish notes):
- SRE (ops): Jonah Li (lead), oncall participants (rotate), responsible for drills and MTTM measurement.
- Observability / Instrumentation: Priya Kapoor (lead), responsible for alert scoring, dashboards, probe coverage.
- Platform & Serving Runtime: Alejandro Ruiz (lead), responsible for gating enforcement, KV cache telemetry hooks.
- Product / Feature PMs: owners for the two pilot services, provide acceptance criteria for user impact.
- Solutions / Customer Success: Samir Patel to coordinate any customer communication paths for Dedicated pilot.

Signal definitions / quick alignment for metrics:
- Availability: successful responses / total requests in 5m windows (exclude client errors in first pass).
- Latency tiers: P50, P90, P99 computed on server processing latency (exclude network egress).
- Error budget burn: rolling 7d and 30d windows using availability objective defined per-service.
- Operational signal for runbooks: time from alert to runbook start, time from runbook start to mitigation action, number of handoffs.

Experiment knobs (things we will try):
- Alert tuning: turn implicit noisy alerts into aggregated scored alerts to reduce false positives.
- Synthetic probes: add targeted probes for prefix-cache warmup behavior.
- Soft gating: route 5-10% of traffic to new model variant and monitor SLO signals before increasing.
- Runbook shortcuts: pre-filled triage templates and an incident 'starter pack' for first responder.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: telemetry gaps for pilot services -> Mitigation: prioritize event capture for core endpoints in Week 0, add lightweight logging hooks if needed.
- Risk: teams overloaded, cannot attend drills -> Mitigation: keep drills short (30 mins), asynchronous playbooks, record sessions.
- Risk: rollout gating automation causes unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: start manual rollback, use conservative thresholds, require 2-person verification for now.

Data collection & evaluation plan (what we will compare):
- Baseline vs pilot: compare 14d pre-period to 14d post-period for P99, success rate, and MTTM.
- Signal of success = lower incident count per 1k deploys + reduction in average P99 spikes.
- Qualitative: feedback from oncall participants on friction and clarity of runbook steps.

Artifacts to produce by end of pilot:
- Pilot retrospective note with measured deltas (metrics + qualitative).
- Lightweight 'how-to' kit for scaling the gating pattern across services.
- Consolidated runbook + cheat sheet + recorded drill.
- Proposal for rollout: recommended thresholds and the next 6 services to onboard.

Open questions & decisions needed (for leadership sync week 0):
- Approval to run canaries on production traffic for Hosted API pilot? (requested: limited 5% windows)
- Temporary SLO relaxations: do we allow small, documented tolerances while instrumenting?
- Resourcing guardrails: confirm 2 days/week from obs and 1 day/week from platform for sprint duration.

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Priya: export baseline telemetry for the two pilot services (due EOD Wed).
- Jonah: draft tabletop script and one-page runbook template (due Fri).
- Alejandro: stub gating policy in Dedicated staging and share example rollout config (due Fri).
- Maya (owner): schedule kickoff + 30-min leadership readout (Tue 10am).

Notes to self / rough ideas for future iterations:
- If runbook stitching reduces handoffs significantly, consider embedding short remediation playbooks in the Console UI for oncall.
- Evaluate a lightweight ML-based anomaly scorer for alerts after we have 4-6 weeks of enriched telemetry.
- Consider a separate mini-sprint to test cost-performance tradeoffs of prefix caching vs model quantization as a follow-up if latency wins are modest.

Appendix: quick glossary (informal)
- Gate vs Gatekeeping: Gate = automated policy that prevents rollout beyond threshold; Gatekeeping = the human + tooling cadence around that gate.
- Bridge-to-green: short checklist to move the service from partial outage to acceptable degradation state.
- Soft gate: canary level with automatic monitoring but manual rollback.

---
End of field notes draft. This is intentionally terse + actionable. Keep comments inline in the doc and I'll iterate after the Week 0 sync.
